issues.justification: The Russian is a famous quoted line and mock-literary phrase; 'vague suspicions' is serviceable but the second instance reads flat. Minor loss of the recurring catchphrase effect, though consistent.

Fine, but earlier 'Якина на кол посадить' is rendered correctly; however the passage 'Лови́т?' was mistranslated as 'Are they hunting them?' losing the sense of Ivan asking whether they are being pursued/caught.

issues.translation_quote: We want a goal! We want a goal!
issues.justification: The crowd's hockey chant 'Шайбу, шайбу' is a culturally specific parody of the 'Tsar, Tsar' chanting; 'We want a goal' loses the puck/hockey reference. Rendering as 'Puck, puck' or 'Pass the puck' would preserve the joke.

issues.source_quote: Служивый люд царя спасенного видеть желает.
issues.translation_quote: The servicemen wish to see the Tsar delivered.
issues.justification: 'Delivered' is ambiguous and awkward; the meaning is 'rescued Tsar'. 'Servicemen' also lacks the archaic flavor of 'служивый люд' (men-at-arms).

issues.source_quote: Вы дo кoтoрoгo часа сегoдня рабoтаете? ... Нет, не знакoмая, нo безумнo хoчу пoзнакoмиться.
issues.translation_quote: This is an actress speaking. No, we haven't met, but I'm dying to meet you.
issues.justification: Source says 'one actress is speaking' in third-person style, fine; but 'Не закрывайте рот!' rendered as 'Don't close your mouth!' is a literal, unnatural rendering of what is a dentist-context joke ('Keep your mouth open!').

issues.source_quote: Ну что ж, придется повысить напряжение. Опасно? Конечно, опасно! Но риск, как говорится...
issues.translation_quote: But, as they say, no risk...
issues.justification: The proverb is 'Риск — благородное дело' (risk is a noble cause); the English 'no risk...' truncates it into the opposite, wrong-sounding proverb 'no risk, no reward' which doesn't match the setup.

issues.source_quote: Иван Васильевич, у нас это не принято. И кильками в наш век отравиться гораздо легче, нежели водкой.
issues.translation_quote: Ivan Vasilyevich, we don't do that here.
issues.justification: Shift of register between Ivan's archaic 'thou' forms and others is mostly handled, but the inconsistent use of 'thou' across Ivan's speech (e.g. 'Then buy them!' / 'Nothing, nothing at all' vs. 'Thou liest') makes the epoch voice uneven.

issues.translation_quote: Now they'll cure you, you alcoholic.
issues.justification: Acceptable; however 'Лови! ... Задавлю, шляпа!' rendered as 'I'll strangle you, you twit!' loses 'шляпа' (dimwit/slob) sense, and 'Логи трубку' wordplay (ложить/класть, incorrect 'lay' vs 'put') is only partly preserved.

issues.source_quote: Что? Нет Иоанна? Да я уже репетировала с ним!
issues.translation_quote: Borisko on the throne? What, you really are rehearsing?
issues.justification: 'Бориску на царство?' is Ivan's archaic reaction to the rehearsal, but 'Borisko' is left unexplained and the cue to the 'Boris Godunov' parody is muddled.

issues.translation_quote: Should eat something with your drink! Faster!
issues.justification: Ungrammatical, subjectless fragment; sounds unnatural. 'We need a bite to eat!' would be natural.
The pun is on a mispronounced French phrase; leaving it as is without any adaptation means the joke (mock-pretentious French) largely doesn't land for English viewers.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Do not order my execution, Great Sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: 'Надежа' is an archaic form of address ('dear lord/liege'); 'our hope' is a literal rendering that sounds odd and loses the respectful archaic address. Repeated frequently.

'Брали квартиру' means 'burgled'; Ivan's reply plays on 'брал' as 'captured' (Kazan taken). 'Did you do' doesn't set up the pun on 'take', so the joke is lost; 'Did you take Shpak's apartment?' would preserve it.

issues.translation_quote: The Tambov wolf is your boyar!
issues.justification: The idiom ('go to hell, you're no boyar to me') is rendered literally and is opaque to English viewers.

issues.source_quote: Вашему изобретению цены нет! Поздравляю Вас! Благодарю!
issues.translation_quote: The wall! Your invention is priceless!
issues.justification: The thief's exclamation 'Стенку!' is attached awkwardly; reading is unclear.

issues.translation_quote: There was a wall here just now!
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Стенка' here denotes a wall unit/partition in apartment; no issue. (Low confidence.)

issues.translation_quote: Knit your brows! Knit your brows!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the German speech is mistranslated/garbled ('Seinen treuen Diener' fragment) and the deliberately comic broken German is not rendered in a way that conveys the joke.

issues.source_quote: Мы его в кипятке и сварили.
issues.translation_quote: So we boiled him in boiling water.
issues.justification: Redundant 'boiled in boiling water'; the original plays the grim joke more tersely ('we boiled him in a cauldron').
